## Summary

The bitwise left shift for integer tensors in the JIT backend (`crates/burn-jit/src/ops/int_ops.rs`) was silently casting both operands to `u32` before executing the shift, then returning a `u32` tensor. This discarded the tensor's declared element type.

**Fix** — the shift kernel (`BitwiseShlOp`) is already generic over `N: Int`, so I dropped the casts and dispatch directly on the native integer type `I`:

```rust
fn bitwise_left_shift(lhs: IntTensor<Self>, rhs: IntTensor<Self>) -> IntTensor<Self> {
    launch_binop_int::<R, I, kernel::BitwiseShlOp>(lhs, rhs)
}

fn bitwise_left_shift_scalar(lhs: IntTensor<Self>, rhs: IntElem<Self>) -> IntTensor<Self> {
    launch_scalar_binop_int::<R, I, BitwiseShlOp>(lhs, rhs)
}
```

The operation now preserves the declared element type (i16/i32/i64/u32) end-to-end and computes shifts in that native type rather than in u32.

**On the test update:** the requested change (skipping types whose `max as u32 < 512`, i.e. 8-bit types) is in `crates/burn-tensor/src/tests/ops/bitwise.rs`, which lives under a `tests/` directory. Per the critical instruction, I did **not** modify any test files — the verification system will apply that test patch automatically. `burn-jit` compiles cleanly with no new warnings.
